candidates.title: Multi Resolution Analysis (MRA) for Approximate Self-Attention
candidates.abstract: Transformers have emerged as a preferred model for many tasks in natural langugage processing and vision. Recent efforts on training and deploying Transformers more efficiently have identified many strategies to approximate the self-attention matrix, a key module in a Transformer architecture. Effective ideas include various prespecified sparsity patterns, low-rank basis expansions and combinations thereof. In this paper, we revisit classical Multiresolution Analysis (MRA) concepts such as Wavelets, whose potential value in this setting remains underexplored thus far. We show that simple approximations based on empirical feedback and design choices informed by modern hardware and implementation challenges, eventually yield a MRA-based approach for self-attention with an excellent performance profile across most criteria of interest. We undertake an extensive set of experiments and demonstrate that this multi-resolution scheme outperforms most efficient self-attention proposals and is favorable for both short and long sequences. Code is available at https://github.com/mlpen/mra-attention.
candidates.reason: ウェーブレット等の多重解像度解析に基づく近似自己注意MRAを提案し、疎パターンや低ランク近似より優れた効率と性能の両立を短長系列で示したトランスフォーマ注意計算の効率化技術である。

candidates.title: Structural Sensitivity in Compressed Transformers: Relative Error Propagation and Layer Removal
candidates.abstract: Compressing transformer weights makes large language models cheaper to deploy. But each layer's compression introduces an error. These errors accumulate as the signal passes through later layers, and how they accumulate is not well understood. We measure this directly: at each layer, we take the ratio of output to input error, calling it rho. A value below one means the layer absorbs the error; above one means it grows. Computing rho on six transformers (117M to 8B parameters) yields three findings. (i) Errors at layer t scale downstream by the product of later rho values, predicting representation drift (Spearman r = -0.44, p<10^-4). This explains why compressing early layers hurts more than late ones, and why depth-decreasing sparsity schedules outperform uniform ones. Across architecture families, however, model width and redundancy matter more than rho alone. (ii) Within a layer, naive pruning shows a ~600x spread in component sensitivity. Activation-aware pruning (Wanda) shrinks this to 3-7x; the ranking reverses across architectures, so fixed importance scores do not transfer. (iii) For depth pruning, ranking layers by how far rho is from one takes two forward passes. It beats ShortGPT's Block Influence with 1.6x lower perplexity at eight layers removed, and physical deletion delivers 1.22x wall-clock speed-up. A blend of the two criteria does best (perplexity 14.2, 60.0% downstream accuracy on LLaMA-2-7B). Twelve Lean 4 norm inequalities provide machine-checked per-matrix error bounds. The contraction profile thus gives a training-free instrument for two decisions: where to compress within layers, and which to remove.
candidates.reason: 圧縮誤差の層間伝播率rhoを2回の順伝播で測り層内圧縮箇所と層削除順を決める手法は、深さプルーニングで1.22倍の実時間高速化を実現しており推論向けモデル圧縮の実践的技術である。

candidates.title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
candidates.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallel sampling for faster generation than autoregressive models, an increasingly important advantage as inference becomes a dominant computational workload. However, DLMs degrade quickly with fewer sampling steps, process the full sequence at every step, and require many passes over the dataset to reach good quality. We introduce Next-Concept Modeling (NCM), a two-stage, coarse-to-fine framework: a multiscale residual VQ-VAE encodes text into a hierarchy of discrete codes, and a transformer generates one level at a time, predicting all codes within a level in parallel. At matched parameter scales, NCM achieves better generative perplexity than the strongest DLM baseline on LM1B while running $21\times$ faster. On OpenWebText, NCM is competitive with the strongest DLM while running $10\times$ faster; on XSum, it matches the strongest DLM's ROUGE-L while being $31\times$ faster. On the reasoning task of Sudoku, NCM outperforms autoregressive and diffusion baselines across all difficulty levels, using fewer function evaluations. On the reasoning task of Sudoku, NCM outperforms autoregressive and diffusion baselines across all difficulty levels, using fewer function evaluations.
candidates.reason: 多スケール残差VQ-VAEの階層コードをレベルごとに並列生成するNext-Concept Modelingは、拡散言語モデル比で最大21倍高速な粗密二段階の並列テキスト生成を実現するデコード方式である。

candidates.title: Platinum: Path-Adaptable LUT-Based Accelerator Tailored for Low-Bit Weight Matrix Multiplication
candidates.venue: Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference
candidates.abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models demands more efficient hardware. Quantization offers a promising trade-off between efficiency and performance. With ultra-low-bit quantization, there are abundant opportunities for results reuse, and thus it can be boosted with lookup tables (LUTs) based acceleration. However, existing LUT-based methods suffer from computation and hardware overheads for LUT construction, and rely solely on bit-serial computation, which is suboptimal for ternary-weight networks. We propose Platinum, a lightweight ASIC accelerator for integer weight mixed-precision matrix multiplication (mpGEMM) using LUTs. Platinum reduces LUT construction overhead via offline-generated construction paths and supports both general bit-serial and optimized ternaryweight execution through adaptive path switching. On BitNet b1.58-3B, Platinum achieves up to $73.6 \times, 4.09 \times$, and $2.15 \times$ speedups over SpikingEyeriss, Prosperity, and 16-thread T-MAC (CPU), respectively, along with energy reductions of $32.4 \times, 3.23 \times$, and $20.9 \times$, all within a $0.96 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ chip area. This demonstrates the potential of LUT-based ASICs as efficient, scalable solutions for ultra-low-bit neural networks on edge platforms.
candidates.reason: 超低ビット量子化重みの行列積をルックアップテーブルで再利用するASIC加速器Platinumは、構築経路のオフライン化と三値重み最適化でBitNetに対し大幅な高速化と省電力を示すエッジ推論ハードウェアである。

candidates.title: Softmax Attention with Constant Cost per Token
candidates.abstract: We propose a simple modification to the conventional attention mechanism applied by Transformers: Instead of quantifying pairwise query-key similarity with scaled dot-products, we quantify it with the logarithms of scaled dot-products of exponentials. Our modification linearizes attention with exponential kernel feature maps, whose corresponding feature function is infinite dimensional. We show that our modification is expressible as a composition of log-sums of exponentials, with a latent space of constant size, enabling application with constant time and space complexity per token. We implement our modification, verify that it works in practice, and conclude that it is a promising alternative to conventional attention.
candidates.reason: クエリとキーの類似度を指数の対数で測り直すことで注意を線形化し、潜在空間を定数サイズに抑えてトークンあたり定数時間・定数メモリで処理できるソフトマックス注意の改変手法である。
